title: hybrid-adaptive-downsampling-and-enrichment-bus-for-console-metrics
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a lightweight, deployable component (the "Enrichment Bus") that sits between the console-ingest gateway and the downstream aggregation/warehouse. Its goals are: 1) perform tenant-aware, policy-driven downsampling to keep hot-path costs and tail latency within SLOs; 2) attach small, deterministic enrichments (tenant metadata, route tags, sample reason) for downstream evaluation; 3) provide graceful spillover and exactly-once semantics for prioritised events when backpressure occurs.

Why this ticket exists:
Current ingest spikes cause bursts of expensive downstream aggregation and storage, increasing unit cost and P95 latency. Existing approaches (global sampling and naive queuing) either lose high-value events or require wholesale upstream scaling. This design balances preservation of high-value signals with cost/latency constraints by making sampling adaptive and explainable per-tenant.

High-level design:
- Hybrid stream-queue: events first land in the low-latency stream (in-memory shard) for the hot-window. Each shard maintains a small LRU of recent keys and a reservoir sampler per-tenant tier.
- Policy engine: tenant config (in Console) defines: hot_window_ms, target_events_per_minute, retention_tier (hot/warm/cold), and anomaly_weighting (optional). The policy engine exposes a lightweight decision API used by the Enrichment Bus.
- Sampling heuristics: combine reservoir sampling for fairness + score-based deterministic retention (e.g., error events, quota spikes, unusual token-distribution) so we preferentially keep high-signal messages. Sampling decisions are recorded as "sample_reason" metadata for downstream audits.
- Enrichment step: attach static tenant metadata (tier, org-id), route hints, and a compact provenance vector (2-3 bytes) to allow later reconstruction of sampling bias in analytics.
- Spillover and persistence: when shard memory exceeds threshold, lower-priority events are demoted to the warm queue on local SSD in compacted Avro/Parquet microfiles; warm persists to S3 after time threshold. High-priority events are checkpointed into an append-only log (Kafka) for guaranteed delivery and reprocessing.
- Fallback: if the Enrichment Bus detects systemic failures (latency > 500ms or storage write failures), it toggles a fallback flag which routes events through the legacy ingest path (full retention) to avoid data loss.

Performance targets:
- p50 end-to-end ingest latency <= 40ms; p95 <= 250ms for hot-window events
- sustained throughput: 60k events/sec cluster-wide; burst smoothing to 200k events/sec with backpressure shaping
- tail event preservation: keep >=98% of events tagged as "high-signal" by anomaly rules
- cost goal: 25–35% reduction in downstream storage and compute for console metrics on typical workloads

Compatibility and integration:
- The Enrichment Bus will expose the existing console-telemetry protobuf schema and a small decision header so existing consumers need only read the new metadata field.
- Integrates with Console RBAC to read tenant retention tiers and with the Console Console (UI) to surface per-tenant sampling logs for customer support.
- Works with current KV cache primitives used by serving runtime: enrichments are lightweight and reference IDs only (no bulky model state).

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests for reservoir and deterministic scoring (coverage for corner cases: cold-start, high-cardinality tenants).
- Staging canary: enable for 5% of tenants, run side-by-side with existing pipeline for 72 hours and compare retention rate and cost delta.
- Chaos tests (write-fail, network partition) to validate fallback toggle and exactly-once checkpointing.
- E2E perf harness that replays production traffic (from anonymized sample) to validate p95 latency under load.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature branch + integration tests (2 weeks)
2) Internal canary (QA + infra) with 0.5% tenants (1 week)
3) Extended canary 5% with active monitoring and rollback automation (2 weeks)
4) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% with cost/latency gates enforced via deploy pipeline

Monitoring and dashboards:
- New Grafana dashboard: grafana.redwood.ai/d/console-enrich/ingest-enrichment-bus (canary vs baseline retention, per-tenant sample rate, p95 ingest latency)
- Alerting: p95 ingest latency > 260ms (P0), hot-window spill rate > 0.5% (P1), fallback-toggle enabled > 1min (P0)

Open design decisions / tradeoffs:
- Reservoir sizes per-tenant: small reservoirs reduce memory but risk missing bursty signals. Proposal: start with reservoir capacity = min(500, target_events_per_minute*0.1).
- Deterministic scoring function: simple weighted sum of anomaly_score + error_flag + rate_delta vs ML model. Start with deterministic rules, measure lift, and add model-based weighting in later cycle.
- Warm-store format: parquet vs compacted JSON-lines. Parquet reduces read costs for analytics but adds write CPU; choose Parquet for warm archives due to downstream BigQuery/warehouse compatibility.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: mis-sampling leads to missed customer incidents. Mitigation: maintain a 24-hour full-fidelity rolling window for a small sample of tenants and expose sampling audit logs in Console.
- Risk: increased operational complexity. Mitigation: clear runbook, fallback toggle, automated canary rollback.

Deliverables / acceptance criteria:
- Enrichment Bus deployed to staging and canary, passing fault-injection tests
- Canary shows >=20% reduction in downstream storage events at parity of critical-signal preservation (>=98%)
- Dashboards, alerts, and a Console UI page showing per-tenant sampling logs
